issue.title: TUI GC policy still permits 32-second main-thread collections and recurrent multi-second hitches
issue.description: Observed after closed epic sase-1ez (2026-10-03). GCPolicy.tick calls collector.collect synchronously; the telemetry provides direct stop duration, while the exact producer of the large cyclic graph remains unproven. Plan a bounded allocation/object-retention investigation across fleet projection and recurring snapshots, compare Python 3.14.7 athena versus 3.12.3 apollo, and preserve memory backstops. Do not merely raise thresholds or move CPython GC to a worker and assume it cannot pause the process. Measure by app instance and revision, compare matched retained intervals and prompt-active/idle behavior, and validate a long-lived representative roster. Large because cause attribution and a measured performance fix require planning; link to closed sase-1ez and related active sase-zn without claiming the latter caused this regression.

task_type_fields.impact: Long-lived TUI processes remain visibly frozen for seconds despite the installed GC policy; idle gating does not bound a collection after input resumes.
task_type_fields.repro: Athena 2026-10-20 epoch 1792496103.287799: tui_gc_pause generation=2 duration_s=32.44874 thread=MainThread trigger=backstop collected=590483, app_instance_id=d2b7cd41 (tui_stalls.jsonl.1 line 1876 in audit snapshot). Related hitch duration=36.954 with gc_overlap_s=33.138 at epoch 1792496105.2534344. A later idle collection took 23.506427s and collected 649759 objects. Retained first sweep counted 329 recovered loop hitches on athena and 185 on apollo, across different retention windows.

issue.creation_reason: A cross-machine production log audit found independently reproducible failures that need durable follow-up.
